description:
Havi Egy Játék Gamejam - Szeptember
Készíts havonta egy játékot és gyűjts össze minden trófea puzzle-t!
2026-ban is folytatódik a Havi Egy Játék gamejam sorozat, melynek lényege, hogy egy hónapod van elkészíteni egy játékot egy adott témában egyedül vagy csapatban. 
Ehavi témák: 
1. Eclipse
2. Swarm
3. Power Nap
Kiegészítő téma:
4. Stealth
// Szabályok
A játék itch oldalának leírásához kérjük használd az alábbi strukturált leírást:
Fejlesztő(k) neve
Választott téma (+ ha használtad a kiegészítő témát)
Miről szól a játék, mit kell csinálni, mi a cél
Irányítás: melyik gomb mit csinál
Külső assetek kreditálása (forrás megjelöléssel)
Illetve ajánlott még kitölteni:
Genre: mi a játék műfaja
Made with: milyen engine-nel készült
Tags: címkék amiken keresztül megtalálható
Average session: milyen hosszú egy játékmenet
Inputs: mivel irányítható (egér, billentyűzet, kontroller)
Olvasd el a részletes szabályokat a honlapunkon: https://www.haviegyjatek.hu/rules
// Meetup és stream
Minden hónap első szerdáján találkozunk és mutatjuk be az elkészült előző havi játékokat. Ugyanígy ott jelentjük be a következő havi témákat is. Az eseményt online streameljük a saját YouTube csatornánkon, illetve ugyanitt visszanézhető is lesz később.
// Kapcsolat
Ha bármilyen kérdésed van, vagy elakadtál, esetleg csapattársat keresel gyere a Discord szerverünkre, esetleg a Facebook csoportunkba. 
Honlap: https://www.haviegyjatek.hu/
Discord: https://discord.gg/nENA76w
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/groups/HEJ.Budapest
Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/@HaviEgyJatek

description:
Hello! Welcome to the entry page for issue #83 Indiepocalypse Zine! 
Is submitting to this jam the only way to submit?
No, just the easiest for me since it organizes everything in one place, works as a form, and is where plenty of people already have their games.  You can always email me directly at indiepocalypse@gmail.com to submit your game as well!
What is this thing anyway? 
Simply, it's a monthly collection of  games from 10 developers all wrapped up in one package. That the developers get paid for! Up front and on the back end! There will also be a short digital zine with a page for each game. Creators are free to design their page to their own liking or submit text and pictures to be laid out for them.
The games are then sold through itch in a single zipped file with a launcher.
You will be paid:
UP FRONT: $20 USD   
BACK END: 5% of sales (before anthology breaks even) | 8% (after)  
Also, I claim no exclusivity or ownership of your games!
Game Requirements
This simply a submission page for the zine. I do not consider it a jam and would encourage others to do the same. If you want to make a new game for the zine (and I'm not commissioning you) more power to you I guess.
-Games can (and should) already be complete and can have been made at any point in time.
-Games can be of any theme   
-Games can be of any length  
-Games can be digital or physical (that can be distributed digitally)  but must be in some way downloadable. This includes mobile games.
-Games can play very loosely with the term 'game'  
-Any number of games can be submitted but each person can only occupy one slot.
-I have no way to play VR-only games, everything else should be fine.
-Make your game playable without me having to find a way load up the project file in whatever engine you made it in
That's pretty much it. Everyone keeps ownership of all their stuff, this is mostly a way to give a platform (and money) to smaller and/or more unknown projects.
How are games selected?
Games are selected by a single curator (me) based on no strict criteria at all. The main goal each month is to make an interesting and diverse zine. Below are some things that I think about when choosing games. Indiepocalypse was created with the intent of being a collection of alternative and outsider works so bear that in mind when submitting. Also, while TTRPGs are accepted (and sometimes even commission) my focus is on the vaguely defined medium of "video games". As such I tend to include 2~3 TTRPGs at most per issue.
This is by no means a list of objectives to meet and there is no objective math way of breaking down and judging a game and anyone who claims otherwise is lying.
-Subjective taste is ultimately unavoidable
-I prefer things that are messy and interesting to ones that are polished and familiar
-Complete is preferable to demos/betas
-Each issue will try to a have a diverse selection of games, even if the 10 best fighting games ever made were submitted only like, 2, would be included
-Length is irrelevant
-I am typically detached from (if not exhausted by) trends in design
-You gotta really try for something if you're making a overhead/twin-stick shooter 
-Execution on intent (or something to the effect) is what I look to when I find a game feels more personally uninteresting than broadly uninteresting (however possible it is to determine such a thing)
What if my game is selected?
After submission entries are curated, if your game is selected, you'll be contacted  and given a form to fill out to collect the materials for the magazine and anything else that may be needed. If you submitted multiple games, you will either: Be sent a message telling you which game was selected OR Receive no additional message and have your choice of bundling the games one entry/choose which game you'd like to be included.
Selections are not made public until the issue is released.  Everyone will receive an email through itch once the games are chosen. If that is the only email you recei

description:
Hi! We're so glad you're interested in joining the World Clean Up Day Game Jam 2026.
Whether you're an experienced game developer, an artist, a musician, or someone making their very first game, you're welcome here. Jam for the Planet is built around bringing creative people together to tackle environmental challenges through games, all while learning, collaborating, and having fun. 
For this jam, the theme is Evolution.
To reflect this, the charity that this jam will be supporting is Conservation International, an organization working to protect biodiversity, restore ecosystems, and support communities on the front lines of environmental change. This means that they will receive 50% of any funds donated by participants or sponsors... whilst the other half will go towards increasing this jams prize pool!
Once the jam ends, all eligible submissions will move into a one-week community voting period. During voting, the queue size will be 6, meaning participants will be shown six games at a time, and the unlock number will be 3, meaning you will need to vote on at least three other submissions before votes on your own game become available.
At the end of community voting, the top 10 submissions will advance to our judging round. Our judges will review each of these games using a detailed evaluation criteria, providing both scores and written feedback across the jam's judging criteria.
Judging will take place over the following week. One week after the judging period ends, the completed rubrics will be returned to the top 10 teams, giving finalists detailed feedback on their games in addition to the final results.
This jam has a total prize pool of 150 USD, from a mix of sources including sponsorships, company partners, and board members. The breakdown is as follows: 
1st place: $75. 
2nd place: $50.
3rd place: $25. 
We have generally been able to pay competitors on their own basis (I.e. if a winner requests pay-pal, we can pay them via that service), but this is subject to change if a method is deemed to be untrustworthy or has associated risk (at our discretion). However, in that unlikely event, we will do our best to find an alternative method that works for both parties. 
To contribute to the overall prize pool for this jam, please call/text us at 202-914-6474, or message an admin on our discord server. 
Want to know more about Jam for the Planet and our mission? Visit our website to learn about who we are, how we donate to charity, and the impact of our game jams. Some information on the website is pending to change. 
Have questions or want to meet the team? Join our discord where you can connect with organizers, chat with fellow developers, and stay updated on all things related to the jam! This is the best place to get your information and ask questions, as our response time is generally faster. 
Our game jam is not just about making games—it's about making a difference. Half of every dollar raised through sponsorships is donated directly to a nonprofit aligned with the jam's theme, supporting real-world environmental initiatives, whether it's reforestation, ocean cleanup, wildlife conservation, or another important cause. 
To donate, please contact us at either jamfortheplanet@gmail.com, call/text our business number (202-914-6474), or message an admin on our discord server.
title: World Clean Up Day Game Jam 2026 ($150+ in prizes)

description:
Kaidan Nights
Urban Legend Visual Novel Jam
Game Theme: Japanese Urban Legends
"The kind of story you might hear whispered in a school hallway, hear about during a late-night sleepover, or stumble across in some forgotten old forum post."
Create a short visual novel inspired by a Japanese urban legend. The entire story should take place over one single night, starting off relatively normal before something strange and unsettling slowly begins to happen.
General Rules
Theme Adherence:
Your game must fit the announced theme and the overall genre of the jam (Horror, Gothic, Dark
Fiction, etc.).
Format: The game
must be primarily a visual novel, interactive fiction, or heavily text-driven narrative game. Mixing
genres (e.g., VN + Point-and-Click, VN + Survival) is completely fine and encouraged!
Fresh Starts: To
keep things fair, the core narrative, script, and code must be created during the jam period.
Assets & Content
Premade Assets:
You are allowed to use free or legally purchased third-party assets (music, sound effects, sprite
packs, fonts, backgrounds) as long as you have the proper license and give credit in your game
description.
Content Warnings:
Because this is a horror jam, you must include a clear Content Warning (CW) list on your game
page and at the start of your game if it deals with heavy, sensitive, or highly graphic
psychological/physical themes.
Teamwork & Submission
Team Size: You can
enter solo or work in a team of any size. There is no limit on team members.
Submission
Deadline: All entries must be submitted before the countdown timer hits zero. Late
submissions will only be accepted under extreme technical circumstances (contact a mod
before the deadline ends).
Keep it Playable:
Please ensure your game has a working build. A web build (HTML5) is highly recommended for
visual novels, as it dramatically increases the number of people who will play and vote on your
game!
Voting & Criteria
After the submission window closes, a public/developer
voting period will open. Games will be rated on the following criteria:
Atmosphere & Tone: How well did the game
capture that eerie, gothic, or terrifying vibe?
Narrative & Writing: Was the story compelling,
spooky, or beautifully twisted?
Use of Theme: How creatively did the team
interpret the jam theme?
Art & Sound Direction: How well did the visuals,
UI, and audio complement the horror element?
Jam Prizes
Discord Feature:
Winning entries will get prominently featured and showcased on our community Discord
server.
YouTube Showcase:
Gameplay clips and highlights of your submissions will be shared on our official YouTube
channel.
Community Growth:
Connect, collaborate, and network with a fresh group of passionate indie narrative game
developers.
Useful Tools
PiskelApp
Pixel Art
BeepBox
Music
GameMaker
Engine
G-Develop
Engine
VN Engines
Ren'py
Visual Novels
Twine
Interactive Fiction
Godot
2D/3D Engine
Jam Requirements
Requirement 1
Submission Rules
Your submission must be a visual novel, set during one night, inspired by a Japanese urban legend, and horror-themed (psychological, supernatural, or folklore).
Requirement 2
Submission Guidelines
Please include a playable build (web builds are encouraged for easy judging), a short description of the legend or rumor that inspired your VN, and content warnings if needed.
Requirement 3
Judging Focus
Submissions will be judged on atmosphere & tone, storytelling, use of urban legend elements, visual presentation, and overall horror impact. This jam is about creativity and mood.

description:
Welcome to Oktrollberfest 2026 Game Jam, we're back again to request, nay, demand you build more troll games! Troll games are games that set up expectations only to subvert them. Submissions are due *before* October this year so that we can stream games in the actual month of October. 
This isn't trollvember despite how cool a month that would be... and, well, Septrollber didn't have the same ring to it.
Judgement
As part of being a participant, you will be provided a form and asked to give feedback to other submitters.
I will stream everyone's web-playable game on my computer, one day in October.
Afterwards, I'll run an awards ceremony and award bespoke, hand-drawn, participation trophies representing folks' contribution to this event. (Drawings like the silly troll at the bottom of this page, but trophies, I don't know)
Rules
Submit a troll game. As much as submitting a game that is not a troll game sounds like it is subverting expectations, you need to understand that not following the rules of a competition on Itch is an unfortunate commonplace problem. We had at least 2 submissions last year that were not troll games and I assure you that doing it again will not subvert my expectations.
Not a game about trolls. I mean, you can, but just to clarify what we mean by "troll game", we specifically mean a game that narratively subverts expectations. E.g., tricks you into thinking you're safe, and you're not! Or tricks you into thinking you're not safe, and you ARE!!! 
Still confusedS earch YouTube for Troll Games for inspiration.
Stanley Parable is probably the most commercially successful game of this genre.
Here's a nearly 3 hour YouTube tutorialfor you to listen to while you work on it!
*Try* to make it web playable (but not required). You're allowed to submit a Windows game, tabletop (rules), etc, but it's possible I won't stream it due to physical limitations on my part.
About this competition
This is a competition's origins is from the somehow still alive in 2026 ZZT Game dev community. If you've found this competition from the wide world of itch, we welcome you!
Don't be surprised if many of your compatriots in this competition are ZZT Game engine games. Everyone is very excited to see you participate with your engine of choice. (You don't need to lampoon ascii / textmode games from the 90s with your entry, yet a bunch of us will be doing so because of the contest's origins)
Curious about ZZT? It's an old-school game engine from the 90s, Epic Games' first game engine! Check out this guide to making a ZZT game if you're interested in learning more.
ZZT entries should submit their games to museumofzzt.com as part of their entry. If you're making a ZZT game please come hang out in the Museum Discord, and if you are uploading to the Museum, please see their upload policy.
